section_summary: These pages document arrangements for Japanese training vessels visiting United States ports in 1936, especially the SHINTOKU MARU in Hawaii and the YAKUMO and IWATE on the mainland. They also record disputes over Japanese sailors joining Seattle’s Fourth of July parade, revised travel plans for Japanese naval officers visiting Canada, and Port Arthur’s request for a future Japanese naval visit.

subfiles.title: War Department view on Seattle parade
subfiles.about: The War Department advises against foreign troops parading under arms on American soil.
subfiles.summary: It leaves participation by Japanese sailors in Seattle’s Fourth of July parade to the State Department but opposes their marching under arms.

subfiles.title: Clarification of War Department parade policy
subfiles.about: The War Department clarifies the exceptions it would allow for foreign troops parading under arms.
subfiles.summary: It disfavors such parades except in special circumstances, including Canadian or Latin American troops.

subfiles.title: American Legion thanks State Department
subfiles.about: Seattle’s American Legion describes arrangements for Japanese participation in its celebration.
subfiles.summary: Sullivan thanks the Department for its help and reports invitations, naval cooperation, police protection, and hopes for goodwill.

subfiles.title: Reply to Major Sullivan on parade policy
subfiles.about: The Department explains the procedure for foreign armed forces to parade in the United States.
subfiles.summary: It says such parades generally are not envisaged; exceptions require advance federal consideration and a formal foreign-government request.

subfiles.title: Cancellation of Ensenada visit
subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador cancels the officers’ proposed Ensenada visit.
subfiles.summary: He asks that United States authorities be notified that Yoshida, Nakamura, Kakuta, and five officers will not visit Ensenada.

subfiles.title: Notice to Labor of Ensenada cancellation
subfiles.about: State forwards notice cancelling the Japanese officers’ Ensenada visit.
subfiles.summary: A copy of the Ambassador’s cancellation note is enclosed.

subfiles.title: Notice to Treasury of Ensenada cancellation
subfiles.about: State forwards notice cancelling the Japanese officers’ Ensenada visit.
subfiles.summary: A copy of the Ambassador’s cancellation note is enclosed.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Ensenada cancellation
subfiles.about: State acknowledges cancellation of the Ensenada visit.
subfiles.summary: The Ambassador is told that interested federal authorities have been advised.

subfiles.title: Customs arrangements for SHINTOKU MARU
subfiles.about: Treasury authorizes customs courtesies for SHINTOKU MARU in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: The Honolulu collector will extend customary facilities during the training ship’s visit.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of NIHON MARU port approval
subfiles.about: The Ambassador thanks State for approving NIHON MARU’s proposed port visits.
subfiles.summary: He acknowledges State’s May 26 note.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard arrangements for SHINTOKU MARU
subfiles.about: Coast Guard units are instructed to assist SHINTOKU MARU in Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Treasury reports issuing instructions for customary courtesies during the August visit.

subfiles.title: Hawaii governor’s office acknowledges visit
subfiles.from: Secretary to the Governor of Hawaii
subfiles.about: Hawaii’s governor’s office promises courtesies at Hilo and Nawiliwili.
subfiles.summary: The letter is forwarded by the Interior Department to State.

subfiles.title: Handwritten Navy memorandum on parade policy
subfiles.from: Office of Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.about: A handwritten note concerns naval parade policy.
subfiles.summary: Its legible portions refer to parades, policy, and a Navy letter.

subfiles.title: Navy policy on participation in parades
subfiles.to: Naval district commandants and fleet commanders
subfiles.about: The Navy lists occasions on which its forces may take part in parades.
subfiles.summary: Permitted categories include national holidays, civic commemorations, patriotic societies, and certain funerals.

subfiles.title: New York special agent on squadron visit
subfiles.about: The special agent describes requested courtesies for the Japanese squadron in New York.
subfiles.summary: He reports the consul’s request, local police practice, and his expectation that the officers would be city guests.

subfiles.title: Protocol Division recommendation for New York
subfiles.about: Protocol recommends allowing the New York special agent to follow customary arrangements.
subfiles.summary: It notes that the warship visits have been approved.

subfiles.title: Instruction to New York special agent
subfiles.about: State asks Burr to make usual arrangements for the squadron’s New York visit.
subfiles.summary: Federal departments and New York’s governor have also been asked to extend courtesies.

subfiles.title: Labor arrangements in Honolulu
subfiles.about: Labor confirms instructions for SHINTOKU MARU’s Hawaii visit.
subfiles.summary: Its Honolulu district director has received appropriate instructions.

subfiles.title: Drafting advice on Nawiliwili
subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs advises postponing a definite response on Nawiliwili.
subfiles.summary: It cites pending reciprocal discussions about American vessels entering unopened Japanese ports.

subfiles.title: Navy objection to Nawiliwili visit
subfiles.about: The Navy approves Hilo but opposes SHINTOKU MARU’s visit to Nawiliwili.
subfiles.summary: It describes Nawiliwili as a small, non-entry port lacking officials to provide facilities and protect United States interests.

subfiles.title: Partial reply on SHINTOKU MARU itinerary
subfiles.about: State approves Hilo and defers its decision on Nawiliwili.
subfiles.summary: The note confirms the planned August dates, approves Hilo, and promises a further communication about Nawiliwili.

subfiles.title: Urgent drafting instruction on Nawiliwili
subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs requests an urgent refusal note for the Nawiliwili visit.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy has asked by telephone for an expedited reply.

subfiles.title: Refusal of Nawiliwili visit
subfiles.about: State declines permission for SHINTOKU MARU to visit Nawiliwili.
subfiles.summary: It cites the absence of port-of-entry status and naval, customs, and immigration officials.

subfiles.title: Request for facts about Seattle parade
subfiles.about: State asks how Japanese personnel actually participated in Seattle’s parade.
subfiles.summary: It seeks details about arms and local reaction.

subfiles.title: Handwritten comment on Seattle criticism
subfiles.about: A file note comments on criticism following Seattle’s parade arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers the criticism unjustified and says Seattle’s initiators got into difficulty.

subfiles.title: Navy forwards confidential Seattle report
subfiles.about: The Navy sends a confidential report on Japanese participation in Seattle’s parade.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure is provided for State’s confidential information and files.

subfiles.title: Commandant’s account of Seattle parade
subfiles.about: The commandant recounts negotiations over Japanese sailors joining Seattle’s parade.
subfiles.summary: He describes local invitations, efforts to obtain federal authority, an initial refusal followed by permission, and Navy assistance during the visit. He argues that prompt State Department replies are important in such cases.

subfiles.title: Proposed acknowledgment of delay
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Affairs and Protocol officials
subfiles.about: Gray proposes acknowledging the need for prompt State action in a Navy reply.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether colleagues object to adding a sentence.

subfiles.title: Advice against accepting sole blame
subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs advises omitting the proposed sentence about delay.
subfiles.summary: It notes delays across several departments and prior oral discussion.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of Navy report
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the confidential Seattle report.
subfiles.summary: Moore also refers to the August memorandum on invitations to foreign armed forces.

subfiles.title: Earlier arrival of SHINTOKU MARU
subfiles.about: The Ambassador reports SHINTOKU MARU will reach Hilo two or three days early.
subfiles.summary: He asks that appropriate United States authorities be informed.

subfiles.title: Early-arrival notice to War
subfiles.about: State relays SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival.
subfiles.summary: The ship is expected two or three days before August 9.

subfiles.title: Early-arrival notice to Navy
subfiles.about: State confirms its telephone notice of SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival.
subfiles.summary: The revised arrival was reported by the Japanese Ambassador.

subfiles.title: Early-arrival notice to Treasury
subfiles.about: State confirms its telephone notice of SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival.
subfiles.summary: The ship will arrive two or three days early.

subfiles.title: Additional early-arrival notice
subfiles.about: State relays SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival to another department.
subfiles.summary: The addressee is illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Early-arrival notice to Interior
subfiles.about: State relays SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival.
subfiles.summary: The ship will arrive two or three days early.

subfiles.title: Early-arrival notice to Agriculture
subfiles.about: State relays SHINTOKU MARU’s earlier Hilo arrival.
subfiles.summary: The ship will arrive two or three days early.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of revised Hilo arrival
subfiles.about: State confirms notifying authorities of SHINTOKU MARU’s revised arrival.
subfiles.summary: It acknowledges the Ambassador’s July 30 note.

subfiles.title: War Department confirms Hawaii cable
subfiles.about: War confirms notification of SHINTOKU MARU’s schedule change.
subfiles.summary: It has cabled the commanding general in Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation about Nawiliwili
subfiles.about: Okazaki seeks a definitive Nawiliwili decision before SHINTOKU MARU leaves Hilo.
subfiles.summary: He reports the ship’s early arrival and likely August 12 departure; Dooman promises prompt word.

subfiles.title: Internal advice on Philadelphia inquiry
subfiles.about: An official suggests obtaining Navy guidance for Philadelphia’s mayor.
subfiles.summary: The note says the proposed reply may give the mayor too little guidance.

subfiles.title: Philadelphia mayor requests guidance
subfiles.about: Philadelphia’s mayor asks how to handle a Japanese consul’s request.
subfiles.summary: He encloses the consul’s letter and asks what accords with State policy.

subfiles.title: Japanese consul requests Philadelphia courtesies
subfiles.about: The consul requests courtesies for a Japanese naval party visiting Philadelphia.
subfiles.summary: About 300 officers and midshipmen plan a sightseeing trip on August 28.

subfiles.title: State’s guidance to Philadelphia mayor
subfiles.about: State advises Philadelphia on receiving Japanese officers and midshipmen.
subfiles.summary: Local authorities may decide courtesies, but State requests that the group not be invited to parade.

subfiles.title: Revised Canada visit of Japanese officers
subfiles.about: The Ambassador revises the officers’ Canada travel schedule and party size.
subfiles.summary: Six officers are now to accompany Yoshida and the two captains, travelling August 28–31.

subfiles.title: Immigration arrangements for Canada return
subfiles.about: State asks Labor to facilitate the officers’ return from Canada.
subfiles.summary: The party is expected to cross at Sainte-Armand and reach New York on August 31.

subfiles.title: Customs arrangements for Canada return
subfiles.about: State forwards revised Canada travel plans for customs arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Yoshida, the two captains, and six officers are scheduled to return by rail through Sainte-Armand.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of revised Canada plans
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the revised Canada trip and confirms arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The note records the larger party and new August 28–31 schedule, and says authorities will extend courtesies on return.

subfiles.title: Further revised Ottawa itinerary
subfiles.about: The Ambassador submits another revised itinerary for Yoshida’s Ottawa trip.
subfiles.summary: He asks that United States authorities be informed.

subfiles.title: Detailed revised Ottawa schedule
subfiles.about: The enclosure lists the party and rail schedule for the Ottawa visit.
subfiles.summary: It names five accompanying officers and routes the party through Boston, Niagara Falls, Toronto, Ottawa, and Montreal.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of further itinerary change
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the final Canada schedule and smaller accompanying group.
subfiles.summary: Five officers, rather than six, will accompany Yoshida and the two captains.

subfiles.title: File note on Port Arthur inquiry
subfiles.about: Dooman checks whether Japanese cruisers can visit Port Arthur.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy says the current schedule does not permit a visit.

subfiles.title: Port Arthur requests cruiser visit
subfiles.about: The chamber asks State to explore adding Port Arthur to the cruisers’ itinerary.
subfiles.summary: It offers to send an invitation through the Texas governor if a visit is possible.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Port Arthur
subfiles.about: State replies to Port Arthur’s cruiser inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The substantive telegram text is illegible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: Treasury authorizes return courtesies
subfiles.about: Treasury authorizes customs courtesies for Japanese officers returning from Canada.
subfiles.summary: The St. Albans collector will grant usual courtesies and free entry privileges.

subfiles.title: Parade-policy memorandum sent to Navy
subfiles.about: State sends an agreed memorandum on invitations to foreign armed forces.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reflects State, War, and Navy discussions.

subfiles.title: Policy on foreign armed forces in parades
subfiles.from: State, War, and Navy Department officers
subfiles.about: The departments set procedures and a general rule for foreign military parades.
subfiles.summary: Invitations must pass through governments and the State Department. Foreign armed forces generally should not parade on American soil, with possible exceptions for Canadian and other American-country forces. The rule covers military units whether carrying arms or not.

subfiles.title: Note on agreement to parade policy
subfiles.about: A file note records interdepartmental agreement on the parade memorandum.
subfiles.summary: It identifies Lincoln, Puleston, and Hornbeck as participants.

subfiles.title: Second copy of parade-policy memorandum
subfiles.from: State, War, and Navy Department officers
subfiles.about: A second copy states the agreed policy on foreign armed forces in parades.
subfiles.summary: It requires government-to-government consultation and generally discourages foreign military parades, while allowing specified exceptions for forces from Canada and other American countries.

subfiles.title: Parade-policy memorandum sent to War
subfiles.about: State sends the agreed parade-policy memorandum to the Secretary of War.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure reflects discussions among War, Navy, and State officers.

subfiles.title: Third copy of parade-policy memorandum
subfiles.from: State, War, and Navy Department officers
subfiles.about: This copy sets out the agreed procedure and general rule for foreign armed forces parading.
subfiles.summary: It directs invitations through State and generally opposes foreign military parades on American soil, with possible exceptions for forces from Canada and other American countries.

subfiles.title: Port Arthur requests cruiser schedule
subfiles.about: Port Arthur asks for the visiting Japanese cruisers’ schedule.
subfiles.summary: Haines refers to State’s August 25 telegram.

subfiles.title: Port Arthur forwards invitations
subfiles.about: The chamber forwards copies of its invitation and request for gubernatorial endorsement.
subfiles.summary: It hopes State will present the invitation to Japan.

subfiles.title: Port Arthur invitation to Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: Port Arthur invites a Japanese naval vessel to visit the port.
subfiles.summary: If the current cruisers cannot come, the chamber requests a future visit.

subfiles.title: Request for Texas governor’s endorsement
subfiles.about: The chamber asks the Texas governor to endorse its invitation.
subfiles.summary: It encloses the letter sent to the Japanese Ambassador.

subfiles.title: State replies with cruiser schedule
subfiles.about: State provides the remaining YAKUMO and IWATE schedule.
subfiles.summary: The current itinerary excludes Port Arthur. State offers to transmit a governor-backed invitation for a future visit.

subfiles.title: Texas governor endorses invitation
subfiles.about: Governor Allred endorses Port Arthur’s invitation to a Japanese naval vessel.
subfiles.summary: He supports the chamber’s request.

subfiles.title: State confirms transmission to Japan
subfiles.about: State reports forwarding Port Arthur’s invitation through its embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The governor-endorsed invitation has been sent to the Japanese Government.

subfiles.title: Instruction to American chargé in Tokyo
subfiles.about: State authorizes presentation of Port Arthur’s invitation to Japanese authorities.
subfiles.summary: Neville is to make clear that the invitation comes from the chamber, not the United States Government.
